source.author: hor
source.text: Virtus est vitium fugere et sapientia prima stultitia caruisse, vides, quae maxima credis esse mala, exiguum censum turpemque repulsam, quanto devites animi capitisque labore; impiger extremos curris mercator ad Indos, per mare pauperiem fugiens, per saxa, per ignis:
source.text_original: Virtus est vitium fugere et sapientia prima / stultitia caruisse, vides, quae maxima credis / esse mala, exiguum censum turpemque repulsam, / quanto devites animi capitisque labore; / impiger extremos curris mercator ad Indos,  / per mare pauperiem fugiens, per saxa, per ignis: /
source.text_english: Virtue is to flee vice, and the first mark of wisdom is to have been free from folly. You see with what great toil of mind and body you avoid what you believe to be the greatest evils: a small income and a disgraceful rebuff. Tirelessly you run, as a merchant, to the farthest Indies, fleeing poverty across the sea, across rocks, across fires.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Et sapientia prima est, stultitia caruisse.
reuse.text_original: Et sapientia prima est, stultitia caruisse.
reuse.text_english: And the first wisdom is to have been free of folly.
